variants.label: LibreGTR detection, instance segmentation and pose

input.name: images
notes: Square input only. Export rejects a non-square imgsz, and height and width are 640 by default.

Pillow computes in fixed point. For an exact match, multiply each weight by 2^22 and round it to an integer, halves away from zero. Start each output sum at 2^21, add pixel x weight in integers, shift right by 22 bits and clip to 0 to 255. Plain float weights differ from Pillow by a level or two on up to about 1 % of the pixels. At the default threshold that stays within the pass bar for every GTR task, but at conf 0.01 it adds two borderline OBB boxes.
Divide by 255 after the resize, then subtract the ImageNet mean and divide by the std per channel.
The export is static: LibreYOLO rejects dynamic=True and half=True for GTR. batch is 1 unless you export with batch=N. A batch=2 export decodes each image like a batch-1 run.
There is no nms=True variant. LibreYOLO rejects it for every GTR task, because embedded NMS export supports YOLO9 detection only. GTR needs no NMS.

outputs.name: pred_logits
outputs.meaning: Raw class logits, sigmoid not applied. queries is 300.

outputs.name: pred_boxes
outputs.meaning: cx, cy, w, h normalized 0 to 1 of the input. The input is a stretch of the whole image, so the same fractions hold on the original image.

postprocess: Apply sigmoid to pred_logits. Flatten the scores to queries x nc pairs and take the top max_det (300 by default) over all pairs, sorted by score. For flat index i, the query is i // nc and the class is i % nc, so one query can yield several classes.
Keep the pairs whose score is above the confidence threshold (0.25 by default). There is no NMS, so the iou argument has no effect.
Convert each kept box to x1, y1, x2, y2, then multiply x by the original image width and y by the original image height. LibreYOLO does not clip these boxes.

outputs.name: pred_logits
outputs.meaning: Raw class logits, sigmoid not applied. queries is 300.

outputs.name: pred_boxes
outputs.meaning: cx, cy, w, h normalized 0 to 1 of the input, as in detection.

outputs.name: pred_masks
outputs.meaning: Raw mask logits per query, sigmoid not applied. mask_h and mask_w are a quarter of the input side, 160 x 160 at 640 x 640.

postprocess: Select detections and map their boxes exactly as for detection: sigmoid, top 300 over queries x nc, keep score above 0.25, no NMS, x1, y1, x2, y2 times the original width and height, no clipping.

Take the mask logits of each selected query and resize them straight to the original image size with plain bilinear interpolation (half-pixel centers, align_corners=False, no antialiasing). OpenCV INTER_LINEAR on the float logits does this.
A pixel belongs to the instance when its resized logit is above 0. The mask is not cropped to the box.

outputs.name: pred_logits
outputs.meaning: Two raw logits per query, sigmoid not applied. The person score is the last one, index 1. Index 0 is unused. queries is 60.

outputs.name: pred_keypoints
outputs.meaning: x0, y0, x1, y1 and so on, normalized 0 to 1 of the input. num_keypoints is 17, in COCO order. There is no box output and no keypoint confidence.

postprocess: The person score of a query is sigmoid of its logit at index 1.
Sort the queries by score, take the top max_det (300 by default, so all 60) and keep those whose score is at or above the confidence threshold (0.25 by default). There is no NMS.
Reshape the keypoints of each kept query to [num_keypoints, 2] and multiply x by the original image width and y by the original image height.
LibreYOLO reports visibility 1.0 for every keypoint, because the graph predicts none.
The box is the extent of the keypoints: min x, min y, max x, max y over the 17 points.

input.name: images
notes: Square input only. Export rejects a non-square imgsz, and height and width are 1024 by default.

This is a letterbox with two differences from the usual one. Scale by r = min(height / h, width / w) and resize to (round(w * r), round(h * r)), where round is Python's round, which sends halves to the even integer. Then paste the result in the top-left corner of a canvas filled with 0 (black), not 114.
Resize with Pillow's BILINEAR filter, with the same per-axis formula and fixed point as the detection variant. OpenCV INTER_LINEAR is not a match when shrinking.
Divide the whole canvas by 255, then subtract the ImageNet mean and divide by the std per channel, padding included. Padded pixels are therefore not 0 in the tensor.
The export is static: LibreYOLO rejects dynamic=True and half=True for GTR. batch is 1 unless you export with batch=N. A batch=2 export decodes each image like a batch-1 run.
There is no nms=True variant. LibreYOLO rejects it for every GTR task, because embedded NMS export supports YOLO9 detection only. GTR needs no NMS.

outputs.name: pred_logits
outputs.meaning: Raw class logits, sigmoid not applied. queries is 300. nc is 15 for the DOTA v1.0 checkpoints.

outputs.name: pred_boxes
outputs.meaning: cx, cy, w, h normalized 0 to 1 of the input canvas, then the angle divided by pi, also 0 to 1.

postprocess: Apply sigmoid to pred_logits. Flatten the scores to queries x nc pairs and take the top max_det (300 by default) over all pairs, sorted by score. For flat index i, the query is i // nc and the class is i % nc, so one query can yield several classes.
Keep the pairs whose score is above the confidence threshold (0.25 by default). There is no NMS, rotated or not.
Map to the original image: multiply cx and w by width and cy and h by height, then divide all four by r. The padding is at the bottom and right, so there is no offset to subtract.
The angle in radians is the fifth value times pi, so it lies in 0 to pi.

Corners: each offset (dx, dy) in (-w/2, -h/2), (w/2, -h/2), (w/2, h/2), (-w/2, h/2) maps to x = cx + dx cos(angle) - dy sin(angle) and y = cy + dx sin(angle) + dy cos(angle). With y pointing down, a positive angle turns the box clockwise on screen.
LibreYOLO's axis-aligned box is the box around those corners: cx plus or minus (|cos| w/2 + |sin| h/2), and cy plus or minus (|sin| w/2 + |cos| h/2). Nothing is clipped.

input.name: images
notes: Square input only. Export rejects a non-square imgsz, and height and width are 640 by default.

Resize with Pillow's BILINEAR filter, with the same per-axis formula and fixed point as the detection variant. On the test image, OpenCV INTER_LINEAR input changes the depth by 4.5 % at the median pixel and by up to 45 % at some pixels.
Divide by 255 only. The graph applies the ImageNet mean and std itself.
Batch size 1 only. Export rejects batch values other than 1 for depth.

In LibreYOLO 1.7.0, LibreYOLO("model.onnx").predict resizes depth input with OpenCV INTER_LINEAR, so its depth maps differ from the .pt model's in the same way. Compare your implementation with LibreYOLO("model.pt").predict instead.
There is no nms=True variant.

outputs.name: depth
outputs.meaning: Inverse depth in 1 / metres at the input resolution, higher is closer. 1 / value is GTR's metric depth estimate in metres. Not normalized.

postprocess: Resize the map to the original image size with bilinear interpolation and align_corners=True: on each axis, source coordinate = destination coordinate x (in_size - 1) / (out_size - 1). OpenCV resize has no align_corners=True mode.
LibreYOLO returns that map as is, as inverse depth with near high. Take 1 / value for metres.

input.name: images
notes: height x width is 1024 x 2048 by default, the Cityscapes canvas. Height comes before width.
Scale by r = min(height / h, width / w), resize to (int(w * r), int(h * r)) with OpenCV INTER_LINEAR and paste it in the top-left corner of a canvas filled with 114.
Unlike the other GTR tasks, this resize is OpenCV, not Pillow. Pillow input drops the pixel agreement with LibreYOLO below 99.7 % on the test image.
Divide by 255 only. The graph applies the ImageNet mean and std itself.
The graph slides 1024 x 1024 windows with stride 768 over the canvas and averages their logits, so a 1024 x 2048 input runs three windows.
The export is static: LibreYOLO rejects dynamic=True and half=True for GTR. batch is 1 unless you export with batch=N. A batch=2 export decodes each image like a batch-1 run.
There is no nms=True variant.

outputs.name: semantic_logits
outputs.meaning: Raw class logits at the input resolution, softmax not applied. nc is 19, the Cityscapes classes.

postprocess: Crop the image area: the top round(h * r) rows and the left round(w * r) columns, where round is Python's round.
Resize the crop to the original image size with plain bilinear interpolation (half-pixel centers, align_corners=False, no antialiasing). OpenCV INTER_LINEAR on the float logits does this.
The label of each pixel is the argmax over the nc classes. LibreYOLO applies no softmax and no threshold.
